newsitem.title: USA: Household in deal with Transamerica - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: Household in deal with Transamerica - WSJ.

text.p: Household International Inc., a consumer-lending and credit card firm, was expected to buy Transamerica Corp.'s consumer-finance business for more than $1 billion, the Wall Street Journal said on Wednesday.
In its electronic edition, the Journal quoted unnamed sources familiar with the deal as saying it was to be announced as early as Wednesday.
The acquisition was expected to be accretive to Households' earnings. Transamerica was expected to use the proceeds to repurchase stock, the paper said.
The acquisition would expand Household's position in consumer financial services, where it already is the No. 2 player in the United States, according to the report.
Combined, the two businesses would have about 970 branches in the United States and would allow Household to cust costs by combining some operations, the Journal said.
Transamerica's consumer-finance business has about $3.6 billion in assets and 420 branches in 44 states.
